prose: Across the ten Assembly elections from 1982 to 2026, Kerala's politics has revolved around two rival coalitions — the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the United Democratic Front (UDF). Over this period the largest front alternated 8 times: the LDF emerged largest in 5 of the 10 elections and the UDF in 5.
Turnout has stayed high throughout, ranging from 71.26% in 1996 to 80.55% in 1987 (measured here as valid votes divided by the electorate).
The sharpest seat swing in the series belongs to 2026, when the United Democratic Front gained 61 seats versus the previous election.

Vote shares between the two major fronts have typically stayed within a few percentage points of each other even when seat tallies diverged sharply — a hallmark of Kerala's finely balanced, bipolar contest in which small swings translate into large changes in seats.
